approaches.title: Destructive node-value marking
approaches.summary: Traverses the list while overwriting each visited node's value with Integer.MAX_VALUE. A repeated marker indicates a cycle, but this mutates the list and can conflict with an existing maximum value.

revisions.shortChangeSummary: Marks visited nodes by changing their values to Integer.MAX_VALUE and detects a cycle when that value is encountered again.

approaches.title: Floyd's tortoise-and-hare algorithm
approaches.summary: Uses two pointers moving at different speeds to detect whether they meet within the list. This determines cycle presence without modifying node data or requiring extra storage.

revisions.commitComment: floyd's cycle finding (slow n fast pointer)
revisions.rawCommitSubject: java 141: floyd's cycle finding (slow n fast pointer)
revisions.shortChangeSummary: Replaces destructive marking with slow and fast pointers; their meeting indicates a cycle.
